stories.head: Adobe CMO Rachel Thornton: AI agents are the new customers brands must sell to
stories.plain: Adobe's enterprise CMO argues that AI agents shopping on behalf of humans are becoming a primary audience marketers must consider. Because agents don't respond to emotion or narrative, the entire creative-and-messaging playbook may need rethinking. This reframes how brands build content, optimize for discovery, and measure persuasion.

stories.head: ADA acquires Algonomy to build a fully agentic retail decisioning platform
stories.plain: ADA bought Algonomy, a specialist in agentic decisioning for retail, expanding its reach to 34 markets across APAC, US, MENA, and Europe. The deal directly connects customer data to automated, real-time action — closing the gap between insight and execution. It signals consolidation around full-stack agentic platforms in retail.

stories.head: Attentive report: 1,050-shopper survey shows personalization is now a baseline expectation in 2026
stories.plain: Attentive's survey of shoppers in the US, UK, and Australia finds that personalized experiences are no longer a differentiator but a minimum requirement driving loyalty and sales. Marketers who treat personalization as optional risk losing relevance. The data gives budget justification for investing in 1:1 messaging infrastructure.

stories.head: Furniture.com on defeating choice paralysis with AI-guided selling
stories.plain: Furniture.com leaders explain how endless product catalogues create friction rather than value for high-consideration purchases. They describe using AI to narrow choices intelligently and guide buyers to decisions. It's a practical case study for retailers rethinking how personalization and agentic recommendations can reduce abandonment.

stories.head: MarTech news roundup: StackAdapt links ad exposure to $4T in card data; holiday buying starts early
stories.plain: Two notable signals from July 30–31: StackAdapt is tying ad measurement to $4 trillion in card transaction data, raising the bar for attribution; and Attentive data shows 83% of consumers plan holiday purchases before Black Friday. Both findings affect how marketing AI is trained, targeted, and evaluated.

stories.head: IAB Tech Lab ships AAMP 2.3 to put AI agents into production advertising
stories.plain: IAB Tech Lab's Agentic Advertising Management Protocol 2.3 adds human approval thresholds on ad spend, privacy controls, and integrations so brands can move AI agents from pilots into live campaigns. This is a governance standard that will shape how every ad-tech vendor builds and sells agentic buying tools — a rare industry-wide rule change.

stories.head: ADA acquires Algonomy to close the gap from data to fully agentic retail decisioning
stories.plain: ADA bought Algonomy, a specialist in agentic decisioning for retail, expanding its reach to 34 markets across APAC, the US, MENA, and Europe. The deal matters because it combines a customer-data layer with real-time AI decisioning in one stack — exactly the architecture enterprise retailers are shopping for right now.

stories.head: Adobe CMO Enterprise: AI agents are becoming brand evaluators and buyers
stories.plain: Adobe's enterprise CMO Rachel Thornton argues that AI agents shopping on behalf of humans don't respond to brand storytelling or emotion — forcing marketers to rethink how they structure product data and digital presence. This reframes GEO from an SEO tactic into a fundamental marketing architecture question.

stories.head: How to measure marketing when AI owns the top of the funnel
stories.plain: As AI answers replace search results, standard click-and-session analytics miss most early-stage brand demand. The piece lays out updated measurement frameworks that capture brand mentions inside AI engines, dark-funnel intent signals, and share-of-voice in generative results — directly changing how marketing teams justify budgets.

stories.head: Yelp integrates reviews and local business data directly into ChatGPT
stories.plain: Yelp's review corpus and business listings are now surfaced inside ChatGPT responses, giving Yelp prime placement in AI-generated local recommendations. For local and multi-location marketers this is a concrete example of how third-party data deals — not just your own SEO — will determine visibility inside AI answers.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents as Autonomous Buyers & Sellers
body: The most disorienting shift of the past 30 days is not AI writing copy — it is AI acting as the customer. Adobe's CMO Rachel Thornton frames this directly: agents are beginning to browse, evaluate, and transact on behalf of humans, which means marketers must now optimize experiences for non-human decision-makers alongside human ones.

The IAB Tech Lab has begun standardizing how AI agents participate in real ad ecosystems, and ADA's acquisition of Algonomy is explicitly aimed at building a fully agentic commerce loop. The strategic decision this forces: do you architect your funnel for people, for bots, or for both — and how do you know which is arriving?
ev: IAB Tech Lab · agents in advertising

themes.head: Measurement Collapse in an AI-Mediated Funnel
body: When AI intermediaries — ChatGPT, AI Overviews, agentic browsers — own the discovery moment, click-based and last-touch attribution breaks completely. MarTech's analysis shows production speed rising fast while measurement practice stagnates; the Prime Day anomaly (9% more clicks, 45% less spending) is a vivid symptom of metrics that no longer map to outcomes.

GrayHair's direct-mail attribution tool and XR/AdImpact's cross-channel political measurement both signal the same underlying anxiety: marketers are scrambling for new signal wherever they can find it. The decision that changes: you can no longer default to ROI models built before AI owned the top of the funnel.

themes.head: Personalization's Intentionality Gap
body: Consumers in 2026 do not just want personalization — they want to feel that the brand meant it. Attentive's research frames "intentional personalization" as the new bar: AI-generated relevance that feels accidental or surveillance-like actively destroys trust, while deliberate, consent-forward personalization builds it as a competitive moat.

MarTech's piece on building advantages AI can't copy and the trust-as-differentiator article reinforce the same point: the personalization arms race commoditizes the technology layer, leaving brand judgment and data ethics as the remaining differentiators. The decision this changes: personalization strategy must now include an explicit intentionality & consent design, not just a segmentation model.

themes.head: Agentic Workflow Integration Hits the Enterprise Stack
body: Agents are no longer pilots — they are being embedded directly into ERP, CRM, and operational platforms at scale. Unanet's expansion of Champ Agents across its full portfolio and KaiNexus pushing AI into operational-excellence workflows show that the agentic layer is moving from marketing point tools into core business systems.

MarTech's guide on directing AI agents and the Salesforce field-service AI paradox both highlight the organizational friction: companies are deploying agents faster than they are building governance, role clarity, or change-management muscle. The decision this forces: who in the org owns agent orchestration, and what human checkpoints remain non-negotiable?
ev: Unanet · Champ Agents across ERP & CRM

themes.head: AI's Accessibility & Simulation Blind Spots
body: Two under-discussed failure modes surfaced this month. First, AI-generated digital experiences are systematically worsening accessibility: AudioEye's research shows that as AI writes more front-end code and UX copy, it reproduces training-data biases that exclude users with disabilities — a legal & reputational risk most martech buyers are not pricing in.

Second, AI buyer-persona simulations miss personality and emotional texture, meaning teams using synthetic audiences to test creative or messaging are optimizing against an incomplete model of real humans. Together, these gaps argue for mandatory human-in-the-loop audits even when AI output looks statistically strong.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack this month, the common forcing function is the same: AI is replacing human intermediaries faster than marketers can rebuild the measurement, governance, and trust frameworks those intermediaries once provided.
